The most important lesson people need to learn is to not provide a conclusion for sticky material. Or only do so when it's not emotionally repulsive. Provide the content and force them to reach their own conclusions. If you wish to lead them in an exchange, ask very leading questions and point out their falsehood when they go astray. This is called the Socratic Method. This forces them to reach discovery on their own terms. Rejecting it means rejecting themselves. Which sets them up for future breakthroughs.

When you force people to reach a conclusion which contradicts their beliefs, even when you have overwhelming facts on your side, you trigger what is called the Backfire Effect. This is fueled by cognitive dissonance and an emotional need to feel one is right and just.

Don't expect to win in a single exchange. It takes time to erode the propaganda amassed in one's head. And by doing this you communicate with people without forcing them into a defensive posture. If they still become defensive it means you are inflicting mental pain upon them, triggered by their cognitive dissonance. But since they are reaching their own conclusion they can't rationally strike out at you and reject your message. If they do, they are doing so irrationally and you have every right to politely point out their error.

The advantage of doing this is that even if you don't "win", others who are simply passively reading in the exchange are also able to reach their own conclusions. In doing so, you are steering many people in the correct direction.

If you are not able to successfully execute this technique, it means either you position is flawed or your approach is incorrect. Which means it's time for introspection and/or research.
